title: The wound goes, the mark remains
odia:
ଘା ଯାଏ, ଦାଗ ଥାଏ
ଲୋକ ଯାଏ, କଥା ଥାଏ।
literal_meaning: The wound goes, the scar remains; people go, words remain.
meaning_odia: ଘା ଭଲ ହୋଇଗଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହାର ଦାଗ ରହେ। ସେହିପରି ଲୋକ ଚାଲିଗଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ କଥା ରହିଯାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଏହା ମଣିଷର ଉପସ୍ଥିତି ଶେଷ ହେଲା ପରେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାଙ୍କ କଥା ବା ତାଙ୍କୁ ନେଇ କଥା ମନରେ ଓ ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ରହିବାର ଚିତ୍ର।
explanation: Each line separates something passing from something that lasts. A scar remains after a wound has gone; words or talk remain after a person has left. The editorial reading extends the bodily image to the persistence of speech and remembrance.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Long after a visitor leaves, the people who met them keep returning to a memorable remark. Someone recalls the second line to describe how the conversation has outlasted the visit.
cultural_context: The repeated ଯାଏ and ଥାଏ give the couplet its parallel structure: departure set against persistence. ଦାଗ makes the first remainder visible; କଥା gives the second a life in memory and conversation.

english_summary: People pass, but words and memories can remain.
